title: Missing values and validation

prerequisite.prompt: Is the text "12" the same type as the integer 12?
prerequisite.answer: No. The first is text and the second is an integer.

vocabulary: A value that was not recorded
Holding a record out because it fails a rule
Which intended records or groups are represented

blocks.text: A fictional activity log contains an absent duration, a recorded zero and an out-of-range value. Our schema accepts exact integer minutes from 0 through 60. Keep rejected records visible for review instead of replacing their values with guesses.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
blocks.text:
rows = [{"minutes": 0}, {}, {"minutes": 12},
        {"minutes": -1}, {"minutes": None}]
accepted = []
rejected = 0
for row in rows:
    value = row.get("minutes")
    if type(value) is int and 0 <= value <= 60:
        accepted.append(value)
    else:
        rejected = rejected + 1
print(accepted)
print(rejected)

blocks.title: Follow the evidence
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right and connect the evidence to the stated rule.

blocks.text: dict.get returns None when this key is absent. An explicit None also represents unknown in this dataset. append adds an item to the end of a list. The script prints [0, 12] and then 3. The exact type check prevents comparing None or text with the numeric range.

blocks.label: Add {"minutes": 60} and {"minutes": "5"}. Predict the accepted list and rejection count.

blocks.text: Using if value would discard the legitimate zero and accept some invalid nonempty text. Test the written type and range rules explicitly. Filling an absent duration with 0 falsely claims an observed zero.
Rejection can change which sessions remain represented. Report 2 accepted of 5 supplied here. A summary of accepted rows does not automatically describe the missing or rejected sessions.

blocks.label: Only 2 of 5 supplied durations were accepted. Why should the report include this?

workbook.title: Distinguish zero and unknown
workbook.prompt: Explain the difference between {"minutes": 0}, {} and {"minutes": None}.
workbook.answer: 0 is a recorded allowed duration. The other two are unknown under this schema.

workbook.title: Trace filtering
workbook.prompt: Predict accepted values and rejections for minutes 4, 0, 61 and "4".

workbook.title: Repair a condition
workbook.prompt: A program uses if value to accept durations. Give a counterexample and the correct rule.
workbook.answer: 0 is wrongly rejected; nonempty text can be accepted. Require exact integer type and 0 <= value <= 60.

workbook.title: Validate independently
workbook.prompt: Write a filter for count values that must be integers from 0 to 10. Process {count: 3}, {}, {count: 0}, {count: 11}, {count: "3"}, using quoted keys in Python. Report accepted values and rejected count.
workbook.answer: Use get, exact int check and inclusive bounds. Accept [3, 0]; reject 3 records. Do not invent values for missing entries.

workbook.title: Report the limitation
workbook.prompt: Only 2 of 5 supplied durations were accepted. Why should the report include this?
workbook.answer: The summary excludes three sessions, which may differ from accepted ones. Report the exclusion and reasons rather than implying full coverage.

teacher.background: Teach Week 14 as a two-session investigation using fictional data. A fictional activity log contains an absent duration, a recorded zero and an out-of-range value. Our schema accepts exact integer minutes from 0 through 60. Keep rejected records visible for review instead of replacing their values with guesses. Assess the three stated outcomes through the independent task, not by copying the worked result.

Collect W4 independently, including code or plan, predictions and explanations, before hints.
Discuss W5 and the exit; use the fresh retry when support was needed.
